SDN.note: The op-ed states nothing on authentication, e-signature services or digital ID.
It names no data centre for hire, tier or cloud region; imported cloud servers are mentioned only in passing.
The author argues for a law and authority to impose localisation; no rule is stated as drafted or in force, and central bank internal requirements are not described.

facts.fact: The analyst Al-Sadiq Mohamed Ahmed writes that Sudan lacks an independent, comprehensive law on personal data protection, and calls for one to be drafted and adopted.
The analyst writes that Sudan has no independent national commission to monitor compliance with data protection.

SDN.note: It states no policy, rule, hosting or contract terms on state data; it criticises payment-switch licences to private firms using imported cloud systems.

facts.fact: The analyst lists the 2007 Electronic Transactions Act among Sudan's existing sector laws, saying it regulates the electronic signature.

SDN.note: It names no nationally owned data centre for hire.
